key_insight: This review traces how materials information extraction has evolved from rule-based pipelines to multimodal LLMs and agentic systems supporting materials discovery.
engineering_relevance: Automated literature extraction can populate materials databases and knowledge graphs, support research assistants, and enable closed-loop discovery when integrated with autonomous laboratories.
method: Review rule-based, NLP, transformer, and LLM extraction approaches.
Examine extraction across text, tables, and figures.
Assess generated datasets, extraction accuracy, computational costs, and pipeline reliability.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a critical assessment of datasets and extraction methods but reports no numerical performance results and identifies a shortage of reliable evaluation benchmarks.
watch_item: Reliable sample-level linkage of structure, properties, processing, and performance remains an open challenge, compounded by inconsistent terminology across document modalities.
paper_title: Automated Materials Data and Knowledge Extraction using Machine Learning and Large Language Models
